papers.title: Continual Learning Mechanisms Compose for Long-Horizon Memorization
papers.abstract: Abstract Composing complementary continual learning mechanisms substantially improves long-horizon memorization in language models by combining data, function, and weight anchors with merged low-rank updates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Language models may need to internalize information that arrives over time and retain it through many subsequent updates. To study this challenge, we introduce long-horizon memorization, a setting in which a model learns 100 query-answer tasks through continual supervised fine-tuning without retaining earlier training examples or receiving task identifiers at inference. Sequential updates cause catastrophic forgetting, and no single continual learning mechanism we evaluate maintains strong retention at this horizon. We hypothesize that mechanisms addressing complementary sources of forgetting will be more effective when composed. We organize these compositions along two design dimensions. Data, function, and weight anchors specify what prior information each update should preserve, while low-rank allocation rules determine where successive updates are retained. To test this hypothesis systematically, we construct three distinct 100-task memorization datasets. We introduce task-level successive halving to search the combinatorial design space and use a factorial experiment to measure individual and interaction effects. Our best method combines all three anchors with merged LoRA, ranks among the top 3 methods in all datasets, and raises average final retention from 1.2% under naive sequential fine-tuning to 34.9%, a 28-fold improvement. The data anchor and merged LoRA provide the largest average gains and interact super-additively on all three datasets. Together, these results show that composing complementary mechanisms substantially improves long-horizon memorization beyond what any individual mechanism achieves.

ru.title: Синергия механизмов: композиция якорей для запоминания в долгосрочном обучении
ru.desc: В статье изучается проблема катастрофического забывания при последовательном обучении языковых моделей на сотне задач без доступа к исходным данным. Авторы предлагают композицию дополняющих друг друга механизмов континуального обучения: якоря данных, функций и весов в сочетании с низкорянговыми обновлениями (LoRA). Они систематически исследуют дизайн этих композиций через факторный эксперимент и поиск методом последовательного халвинга на трёх наборах данных. Лучший метод повышает сохранение знаний с 1,2% до 34,9%, демонстрируя, что комбинирование механизмов, адресующих разные источники забывания, даёт синергетический эффект.

en.title: Boosting Memory in Language Models with Combined Learning Strategies
en.desc: This paper discusses how to improve long-term memory in language models through a combination of different continual learning strategies. It introduces the concept of long-horizon memorization, where models learn multiple tasks without retaining previous examples. The authors propose using complementary mechanisms, such as data, function, and weight anchors, along with low-rank updates, to enhance memory retention. Their experiments show that this combined approach significantly increases retention rates compared to traditional methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating various strategies in continual learning.

zh.title: 组合互补机制提升长期记忆能力
zh.desc: 本文探讨了在语言模型中，通过组合互补的持续学习机制来显著提高长期记忆能力。研究表明，模型在没有保留早期训练样本的情况下，通过持续的监督微调学习多个查询-回答任务时，容易出现灾难性遗忘。我们提出了一种新的方法，通过数据、功能和权重锚点的组合，以及低秩更新，来有效地保留重要信息。实验结果显示，最佳方法将最终记忆保持率从1.2%提高到34.9%，证明了组合互补机制在长期记忆中的有效性。

papers.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce and release ScienceBuddy, an interactive scientific research workspace that brings continually improving scientific agents into researchers' everyday workflows. ScienceBuddy supports researchers in carrying out scientific tasks while transforming their requests, feedback, and execution evidence into tasks and evaluation rubrics for continual learning. At its core is recursive-in-recursive self-improvement, a paradigm that couples harness evolution with model reinforcement learning: the inner recursion improves the harness with the model fixed, while the outer recursion trains the model under the improved harness. Harness evolution shapes training experience, and model learning creates new opportunities for harness adaptation. We present case studies of researcher interaction, harness refinement, and model learning, with the benchmark cases spanning four scientific task families. By releasing ScienceBuddy as a research product, we make this paradigm available to the scientific community and take a step toward discovery intelligence: scientific AI that advances through sustained collaboration with researchers and evolves alongside the research it supports. Website: http://science-buddy.io

ru.title: Научный ассистент с самооптимизацией через взаимодействие с исследователями
ru.desc: В работе представляется ScienceBuddy — интерактивная рабочая среда, которая интегрирует научных агентов в повседневный процесс научных исследований. Система преобразует запросы исследователей, их обратную связь и результаты выполнения в задачи для обучения модели. В основе подхода лежит парадигма рекурсивной самооптимизации: внутренняя рекурсия улучшает механизм исполнения при фиксированной модели, а внешняя рекурсия обучает модель на основе улучшенного механизма. Такая синергия между эволюцией архитектуры и обучением модели с подкреплением позволяет создать научный AI, который развивается в сотрудничестве с исследователями.

en.title: Empowering Researchers with Evolving AI Tools
en.desc: ScienceBuddy is an interactive platform designed to assist researchers in their scientific tasks by integrating intelligent agents that learn and improve over time. It utilizes a unique approach called recursive-in-recursive self-improvement, which combines harness evolution with model reinforcement learning to enhance both the tools and the learning models. This system allows for continuous adaptation and refinement based on researcher feedback and task execution evidence. By providing case studies across various scientific tasks, ScienceBuddy aims to foster a collaborative environment where AI evolves in tandem with scientific research.

zh.title: 科学研究的智能助手
zh.desc: 我们介绍了ScienceBuddy，这是一个互动的科学研究工作空间，旨在将不断改进的科学代理融入研究人员的日常工作流程中。ScienceBuddy支持研究人员执行科学任务，同时将他们的请求、反馈和执行证据转化为任务和评估标准，以实现持续学习。其核心是递归中的递归自我改进，这种范式结合了进化的利用与模型强化学习：内层递归在固定模型的情况下改进工具，而外层递归则在改进的工具下训练模型。通过发布ScienceBuddy作为研究产品，我们使这一范式可供科学界使用，朝着发现智能的方向迈出了一步：科学AI通过与研究人员的持续合作而不断进步，并与其支持的研究共同演变。

papers.title: AI for Games in the Foundation Model Era
papers.abstract: Abstract  Foundation models, alongside advances in learned game-world models, are reshaping AI across the game lifecycle. Beyond playing games, recent systems model players and game dynamics, support design and development, adapt player-facing experiences at runtime, and evaluate resulting artifacts. Yet these directions have evolved largely separately, obscuring which capabilities transfer across settings and which remain tied to particular games, engines, interfaces, or player populations. We organize the literature into six roles according to the immediate use of AI output: playing and acting; modeling players and games; designing games; building and maintaining games; generating and adapting at runtime; and testing and evaluating games. For each role, we examine what structure is supplied by the game or workflow, what AI learns or produces, which capabilities and artifacts transfer across settings and roles, and what evidence supports the claims. We identify cross-role connections: trajectories train world models, learned environments provide experience for agents, design specifications drive executable implementations, and play or testing feedback guides revision. However, control schemes, rules, engine interfaces, state representations, and player contexts often remain setting-specific, so downstream claims require validation in the target setting. Evaluation is most standardized for bounded game playing and selected learned environments, while persistent state in learned worlds, repeated software revision, validated player modeling, sustained runtime adaptation, and representative automated testing remain less established. The central challenge is to reuse or transfer outputs and capabilities across roles while re-establishing evidence for effectiveness in the game-specific contexts where they are used.

ru.title: AI в игровой индустрии: от единых моделей к переносимым решениям
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается применение фундаментальных моделей и обученных моделей игровых миров на протяжении всего жизненного цикла видеоигр. Авторы систематизируют литературу по шести ролям использования AI: игровой процесс, моделирование игроков и игровой динамики, дизайн, разработка, генерация и адаптация во время игры, тестирование. Исследование выявляет связи между этими ролями через траектории обучения, обученные окружения и спецификации дизайна, но отмечает, что управление, правила и интерфейсы часто остаются специфичными для конкретной игры. Основная проблема заключается в переносе возможностей AI между разными ролями с сохранением эффективности в контексте конкретных игр.

en.title: Transforming AI Across the Game Lifecycle
en.desc: This paper discusses how foundation models and advanced game-world models are changing artificial intelligence (AI) in gaming. It categorizes AI applications into six roles, such as playing games, modeling players, and designing games, to understand how AI can be utilized throughout the game lifecycle. The authors highlight the importance of transferring AI capabilities across different gaming contexts while also noting that certain aspects remain specific to individual games or systems. They emphasize the need for validation of AI outputs in the specific settings where they are applied, particularly in areas like player modeling and runtime adaptation.

zh.title: 重塑游戏AI：跨角色能力的转移与验证
zh.desc: 基础模型和学习的游戏世界模型正在重塑人工智能在游戏生命周期中的应用。除了玩游戏，最近的系统还能够模拟玩家和游戏动态，支持设计和开发，并在运行时调整玩家体验。尽管这些方向在发展上相对独立，但我们可以将文献组织成六个角色，分析AI输出的直接用途。主要挑战在于如何在不同角色之间重用或转移输出和能力，同时在特定游戏上下文中重新建立有效性证据。

papers.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
papers.abstract: Abstract Gavel extracts skill-routing signals from frozen LLM hidden states via lightweight linear projections to select tools without external retrieval or context overload.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Skills extend an LLM agent beyond its parametric knowledge, and the gain they promise rests on picking the right one. Deployed harnesses route by preloading every skill's metadata into the context, which disperses the agent's attention and caps the library size. Retrieval pipelines move the selection out of the context, but also out of the agent's capability. We show that the frozen agent LLM already carries the routing signal in its own forward passes, and that two linear maps suffice to read it out with no skill text in the context. Gavel (Glance And Verdict from a frozen LLM) reads it in two steps. A glance projects the task's and each skill's mid-layer states through the two maps, the only parameters trained, and scores the full library against compact per-skill banks that one forward pass builds at installation. A verdict then resumes the shortlisted skills' forward passes and reads the model's own likelihood and yes/no judgment, fused with the glance as a product of experts. Trained once, Gavel transfers zero-shot to three public benchmarks and SkillTraj, our new benchmark of 372 simulated agent trajectories. On Qwen3-32B it outperforms progressive disclosure and retrieve-and-rerank pipelines that add 1.2B to 16B external parameters, by up to 13.4 points on written tasks and up to 21.9 when the need for a skill arises mid-rollout. Routing accuracy improves as the backbone does, and in a bash-agent harness the same 32B triggers the correct skill on Skill-Use more often than far larger frontier models running in Codex.
affiliations: Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences, Tsinghua University

ru.title: Выбор навыков без контекста: маршрутизация через внутренние представления LLM
ru.desc: Gavel — это метод маршрутизации навыков в агентах на основе LLM, который использует лёгкие линейные проекции скрытых состояний замороженной нейросети для выбора нужного инструмента без дополнительного поиска информации. Вместо того чтобы загружать метаданные всех доступных навыков в контекст, система учится извлекать сигналы маршрутизации непосредственно из промежуточных слоёв LLM через две обучаемые линейные карты. Подход состоит из двух этапов: сначала модель оценивает релевантность каждого навыка, а затем на основе этих оценок выбирает наиболее подходящие кандидаты для дальнейшей обработки. Экспериментально показано, что Gavel превосходит существующие методы маршрутизации на нескольких бенчмарках и переносится на новые задачи без переобучения.

en.title: Gavel: Smart Skill Selection from Frozen LLMs
en.desc: The paper presents Gavel, a method that extracts skill-routing signals from the hidden states of a frozen large language model (LLM) using lightweight linear projections. This approach allows the LLM agent to select appropriate tools without relying on external retrieval systems or overwhelming context. Gavel operates in two steps: first, it projects the task and skill states to score potential skills, and then it evaluates the shortlisted skills to make a final decision based on the model's own likelihood judgments. The results show that Gavel outperforms traditional retrieval methods and scales effectively across various benchmarks, demonstrating improved routing accuracy with larger backbone models.

zh.title: Gavel：高效技能路由的创新方法
zh.desc: Gavel是一种从冻结的LLM隐藏状态中提取技能路由信号的方法，使用轻量级线性投影来选择工具，而无需外部检索或上下文过载。它通过预加载每个技能的元数据来分散代理的注意力，并限制库的大小。Gavel通过两步读取路由信号，首先通过线性映射投影任务和技能的中间层状态，然后根据模型的判断进行筛选。经过一次训练，Gavel在多个基准测试中实现了零-shot转移，表现优于传统的检索和重排名管道。
